newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INSTANT VIEW - Brazil sets new large forex band.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Brazil sets new large forex band.

text.p: Following are economists' comments on Brazil's new large foreign exchange rate band, which was lowered on Tuesday to between 1.05 reais and 1.14 reais per dollar from 0.97 and 1.06 reais per dollar.
MARCELO CARVALHO, chief economist for J.P. Morgan in Brazil: "This means no change in exchange rate policy. The policy of a mini-band remains in place."
Carvalho said the new band would allow for a 7.4 percent devaluation of the reais currency over a 12-month period.

"They lowered the floor by 7.2 percent and the ceiling by 7.6 percent, giving you a 7.4 percent depreciation over 12 months or 0.60 percent a month. This is one more piece of evidence to believe in the current exchange rate policy," Carvalho said.
The Central Bank has been devaluing the reais against the dollar by between 0.50 percent and 0.65 percent over the past several months.
It depreciated the reais by 6.9 percent against the dollar last year.
MATTHEW TAYLOR, economist at Trend Analise in Brazil:
"The market was expecting this. It signals no acceleration in the depreciation of the real and monthly depreciations should continue at about 0.60 percent against the dollar."
Taylor expected the new band to last about 12 to 15 months, resulting in a 1997 depreciation of the real of between 7.0 percent and 7.4 percent against the dollar.
The previous band was set on Jan 30, 1996, lasting a little over 12 months.
MARCELO ALLAIN, chief economist at Brazilian bank BMC: "Nothing has really changed. They maintained the same nine centavo spread in the large band."
Allain added: "The Central Bank will continue to administer exchange rate policy through the mini-band system."
"The only new thing is (that) the Central Bank annoucned a new change in the mini-band along with announcing the new large band," he said.
DANY RAPPAPORT, chief economist MCM Consultores: "This is well within market expectations. This doesn't change our estimate for a 7.2 percent depreciation of the real against the dollar in 1997."
Rappaport said the new large band would probably remain until April or May of 1998.
